AiRecommendationItem.x-ticvai-persistence: none — held in jsonb on ai.rec_decision.items, through AiRecommendationItemList
AiRecommendationItem.description: One recommended item. **Carries a Pricing price reference, never a computed price** (AIR-029).

trackingId.description: Echoed on every `recordRecommendationEvents` event and as `orders.addCartLine.recommendationId`, so attribution never guesses.

productId.description: The product recommended. **Exactly one of `productId`, `promotionId` or `couponRef`, `rewardId` or `challengeId` is set, by `kind`** (29 September, build): `offer` carries a promotion or coupon, `reward` a loyalty reward, `challenge` a challenge, every other kind a product.

variantId.description: **What the guest adds to the cart, when there is nothing to choose** (r8, ORDERS-MONEY-C40, the lead's option A): for a product item whose product has one default variant, that variant, resolved from the Pricing price reference the item carries; the add-to-cart asks only the quantity (and a date for a timed product). Null when the product has several variants: the screen lets the guest choose (`catalogue.listProductVariants`, option B). Null on non-product kinds (offer, reward, challenge), which have their own action, never addCartLine.

performanceId.description: For a timed product with exactly one bookable performance in the context the engine was given (the cart's date), that performance (r8, ORDERS-MONEY-C40); otherwise null and the screen asks for the date.

promotionId.description: For `offer`, a published promotion the guest is eligible for. Promotions computes the discount at the basket, never the engine.

couponRef.description: For `offer`, a coupon campaign; a code is assigned only when the guest takes it (`promotions.assignCoupon`).

rewardId.description: For `reward`, a marketing-crm loyalty reward the guest can redeem.

challengeId.description: For `challenge`, a marketing-crm challenge the guest can join.

priceRef.description: The Pricing reference the channel resolves to a price. AI never computes a price.

reasonTemplateKey.description: The template reason (decided 29 September, decision 9): no model writes guest-visible reasons.

reasonText.description: The rendered template in the session locale, where the channel shows reasons.

confidenceBand.description: Design 5.6: a band, never a bare percentage.

score.description: Normalised score. **Returned to staff callers only**; a guest response omits it.

AiRecommendationResult.x-ticvai-persistence: none — written as ai.rec_decision after the response
AiRecommendationResult.description: The recommendation slot's content (design 2.2 A). Empty `items` is a valid answer: the slot stays empty.

BookingFlow.description: **A venue's booking flow (decided 29 September, W12: operators pick their flows, see which steps are required, set their own order).** Made from a `BookingFlowType`; lives in the working draft and reaches guests with `publishTenantConfig`, which copies the venue's flows into the version's snapshot. A product or category names its flow (catalogue `bookingFlowId`); otherwise the venue's default for the type serving its kind applies.

name.description: Staff-facing, e.g. "Day pass, date first". Not shown to guests.

isDefaultForType.description: At most one per venue and type; setting it takes it from the previous default.

isEnabled.description: A disabled flow is kept and not published; products naming it fall back to the default.

steps.description: Every step of the type, in the venue's order. Filled from the type when left out on create.

isValid.description: Whether the flow passes `validateBookingFlow`; worked out in the same transaction as each write. `publishTenantConfig` refuses a draft holding an invalid enabled flow.

scopePath.description: The partition key (ADR-0005). Written at `venue` scope.

BookingFlowLevelSettings.description: **The settings that belong to one flow, not to the venue (decided 29 September, W12).** Moved here from `BookingFlowSettings`, which keeps the venue-wide ones. Each keeps its rev 3 meaning and default. A field left out takes its default.

performanceReveal.description: **Performance reveal (rev 3 REV3-2).** `dateTimeTicket` shows the times only once a date is picked and the tickets only once a time is picked; `allAtOnce` shows them together. Product-first (W8) is the step order of `experienceWorkshop`, not a value here.

signInAt.description: **Where the guest is asked to sign in, or for a guest-checkout code (rev 3 REV3-3).** `afterAddOns` asks as the guest leaves the extras step; `atPayment` asks at payment. The basket is kept either way.

seatEventDateMode.description: **Date and time on a seated event (rev 3 REV3-4).** `inlineStep` asks for them before the seat map; `popupOnSeatMap` opens the seat map with a date and time pop-up. Read only by the seated flow types.

extrasStep.description: `auto` shows the extras step only when the cart's products have add-ons; `never` is the same as turning the optional `extras` step off.

quickTour.description: **Quick tour (rev 3 REV3-20).** A first visit gets a coach-mark tour of this flow's steps, replayable from a Quick tour button. Seen-state kept on the device only.

consentQuestionIds.description: **The flow's own consent questions (rev 3 REV3-26).** Asked on every booking through this flow, together with those of each product in the cart, each question once. Each id names an active `ConsentQuestion` of the tenant in marketing-crm, or 400. A Help me choose answer may pre-fill one (`GuidedChoice` `consentPrefill`); the guest still confirms it.

BookingFlowStep.description: One step of a venue's flow, in the venue's order (decided 29 September, W12).

scopePath.description: Where the row is owned: the path of the scope that wrote it (its venue, or the region or tenant that configured it), set by the server from the caller's scope and never taken from a request. Row-level security reads it, so a venue writes and reads its own rows (MOD audit, 14 October 2026, CHG-MOD-007).

enabled.description: A `required` step cannot be off; the flow saves and `isValid` turns false.

requirement.description: From the flow type, so the CMS can mark the step without a second read.

settings.description: The step's own settings, by the names the type's `stepSettings` gives for this step (e.g. `languages` on `language`, `minHours` on `duration`). A name the type does not give is refused with 400.

BookingFlowTypeKey.description: **The flow types the system catalogue offers (decided 29 September, W12; impact.md b).** `seatedFixedPerformance` and `seatedDateTimeSeatMap` are the two seated flows; `cabanaMap` is the one cabana flow (W6; `cabanaBySize` was removed in r8: a guest books a cabana from the map only, lead decision of 20 October 2026); `experienceWorkshop` puts the product before the date (W8); `multiLocation` opens on the location switcher.

budgetSpent.description: BL-169. **A campaign could spend without limit** — following the promotions `budgetCap` precedent. **Sending stops at the cap rather than overspending and reporting it**, because a marketing budget discovered after it was exceeded is a budget nobody set.

sentCount.description: **How many messages went out**, counted from `marketing.message_dispatch` at read time rather than kept as a counter on the campaign row, so it cannot drift from the dispatch records it summarises. Test sends are not dispatches of the campaign and are not counted.

mergeDefaults.description: Fallback values for the template's `mergeFields`, by name, used where a guest has no value.

promotionId.description: Offer carried by the campaign. Coupon codes are issued from it.

event.description: `entitlementExpiring` (29 September, build pass, group G2; 5.5.30) fires on `entitlement.expiringSoon`: a ticket or pass the guest still holds comes within its template's `expiryNoticeDays` of `validTo`. The notice period is set on the template, so `delayHours` shifts the send within it rather than setting it. An entitlement belonging to a membership is left to `membershipExpiring`, so a member is not told twice.

CatalogueImportJob.description: 1.4.2. **Two-phase, following `seating.ImportJob`** — and carrying the same lesson: a job that parses zero products is not a parsed job.

findings.description: **What an operator sees before committing** — missing prices, duplicate codes, unknown categories, codes that do not match the tenant's schema.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `venue` scope.**

jobKind.description: **One job table for every catalogue bulk operation** (29 September, data model DM3): product import (the original use), environment transfer (ADM-124) and bulk pricing update or import (ADM-080). A pricing job never writes prices; committing it creates a change request (`changeRequestId`).

parameters.description: Bulk pricing: `{selectBy, selectionValues, operation, adjustmentPercent, adjustmentAmount, targetCurrency, effectivePeriodFrom, effectivePeriodTo}`.

CatalogueState.x-ticvai-persistence: none — computed from catalogue.bundle_application, the workstation's latest applied report (CHG-R8MIG-015)
CatalogueState.description: The workstation's local catalogue position. A terminal beyond `staleAfter` must refuse to trade rather than transact against stale prices. **Read from Catalogue** (R8 blocker FOUNDATION-AI-C44, CHG-R8MIG-015): the workstation's latest `applied` row in `catalogue.bundle_application` (catalogue#bundleApplicationRecords) gives `appliedBundleVersion` and `appliedAt`, that bundle's `catalogue.published_bundle.stale_after` gives `staleAfter`, and the venue's newest published bundle, when newer, is `pendingBundleVersion`.

staleAfter.description: Beyond this the terminal refuses to trade.

ConsentPurpose.description: `storedPaymentCredential` (a card saved for later, `storePaymentToken`) and `facePassEnrolment` (a face enrolled for entry, `enrolFacePass`) are purposes of their own (R8 blocker ORDERS-MONEY-C21, CHG-R8MIG-022), so a screen picks the row by its purpose instead of guessing: each tenant has one `marketing.consent_purpose` row of each, seeded with the tenant's other purposes.

sendWindow.description: Hours during which sending is permitted. A promotional message at 3am is a complaint waiting to happen.

sendTimeMode.description: `optimised` sends each recipient at the hour `ai.requestSuggestion` (kind `sendTime`) gives for them, inside `sendWindow` (29 September, build pass, group G2; 22.3.19). `fixed` is the behaviour before. Falls back to `scheduledFor` per recipient where there is no suggestion or AI is off.

optimiseChannel.description: With `sendTimeMode` `optimised`, route each recipient to the channel the suggestion names, among the channels they consented to (22.9.16). Off keeps `channel`.

variants.description: **A/B (or up to five-way) content and subject variants** (29 September, build pass, group G2; 22.1.17, BO-772). Each is a subject override and optionally a different template, written by a person or taken from an AI draft (`ai.proposeMarketingContent`, `source` `aiDraft`). Held as rows of `marketing.campaign_variant`. Null or empty is a single-content campaign.

abTest.description: How the variants are tested. Required when `variants` has two or more.

testPercent.description: Share of the audience the variants are tested on; 100 splits everyone and picks no winner.

minimumSamplePerVariant.description: Below this many sends per variant no winner is declared automatically; a person picks.

winningVariantId.description: Set by the automatic rule, or by a person through `updateCampaign`.

ruleGroups.description: **Nested AND / OR / NOT groups** (contract gap CHG-WIR-007, BO-755; CHG-CSA-045). Where present, the segment matches `criteria` (combined by `match`) AND every group here. Absent keeps the flat list.

effectiveFrom.description: The segment is evaluated for sends only from this time.

ownerPrincipalId.description: Who answers for the segment; defaults to its creator.

requiresApproval.description: Where true, a campaign may use the segment only after an `approvals` request on it is approved.

DeploymentProfile.description:
How this workstation obtains catalogue and inventory (ADR-0013).
- `terminalLocal` — own SQLite, leases direct from the cell. Small venues, 4G sites - `venueEdge` — own SQLite, distributed via the venue edge node which holds the
  venue lease and sub-leases to terminals. Mid and large venues, stadium gates
- `thin` — no local catalogue, server reads. Non-transactional surfaces only

DeviceBinding.description:
A device as its workstation is configured with it. **Binding a device here moves its row to the workstation's scope**: `platform.device.scope_path` becomes the workstation's path, so the device's own session, scoped to that workstation, can write its heartbeat (ADAM CR-095, CHG-RSF-001).

**A registered device linked to the workstation** (ADAM CR-155, option A, 18 October 2026; CHG-CRA-004). `deviceId` names an existing `platform.device` (registered by `registerDevice`); in `configureWorkstation` it is what links the device (`platform.device.workstation_id`, `isRequired`). `kind`, `driver` and `identifier` are the device's own record, returned on `Workstation.devices`; a request's values for them are not written.

deviceId.description: **The registered device** (CR-155): the `platform.device` row's own id. Every item `configureWorkstation` is sent names one; an item without one, or naming no registered device of this tenant, is `422 unknown-device`.

driver.description: Driver identifier. Adding a vendor is a driver plus configuration, never a core change — every venue arrives with hardware not previously seen.

isRequired.description: When true, the workstation refuses to open a shift if the device is absent.

beneficiary.description: Who the money is for. Shown to the guest, and it is the reason they give.

liabilityAccountId.description: **Donations post here, not to revenue** (1.1.132). Money collected for a charity is not the venue's to recognise, and treating it as revenue is a restatement waiting to happen.

channels.description: 1.1.133. Where it may be solicited — POS, kiosk, web, app.

raisedTotal.description: **Not reversed when the campaign closes.** The money is still owed.

description.description: **Validity, re-entry and transfer rules in prose.** "Can I leave and come back" is answered from here, and a name cannot answer it.

id.description: Assigned by the server on create; `createEntitlementTemplate` does not take it.

daysOfWeek.description:
1.1.7 and 1.1.82. **A camp ticket admits on Tuesdays and Thursdays for six weeks**, and `validityKind` had six values with no day pattern among them.
The shape is settled elsewhere in the package — `fnb.MenuAvailability` and `promotions.PromotionConditions` both carry it. **Null means every day**, which is what every existing entitlement means today.

expiryAnchor.description:
1.1.90 to 1.1.92. **A pass bought on the 20th and expiring on the 31st cannot be expressed by an offset in days.** `offsetDays` is the existing behaviour and stays the default.
`seasonEnd` anchors to the venue's own season rather than the calendar — a water park closing in October is not a quarter boundary.

expiryDate.description: Where `expiryAnchor` is `fixedDate`. Every pass expires the same day regardless of purchase.

expiryNoticeDays.description: **How many days before `validTo` access raises `entitlement.expiringSoon`** for an entitlement of this template still `issued` or `partiallyConsumed` (29 September, build pass, group G2; 5.5.30). What a pre-expiry message or campaign is triggered by. Null, the default, means no notice: a day ticket needs none, an annual pass might want 30. An entitlement bought inside its own notice period raises nothing.

carriesStoredValue.description:
BL-033. **A ticket that is also a wallet** — a resort pass with 200 dirhams of spend on it, deducted at a gate or a till.
**The value is a `retail.Wallet` bound to the entitlement, not a balance on the ticket.** One balance mechanism (CF-126), so it holds authorisations, expires by credit type and appears in the same reports — a second balance on the entitlement would have been the seventh implementation.

validTimeWindows.description:
BL-036, 1.1.81 and 1.1.83. **A time-window entitlement needed a performance to express** — valid 09:00 to 13:00 on any day was a thing you built by creating performances.
**A window is a property of the entitlement and a performance is an occurrence**, and conflating them means a morning pass generates 365 performances a year.

blackoutDates.description: **Calendar exceptions on the entitlement.** An annual pass excluding public holidays is the normal case and had nowhere to live.

fastTrackTier.description:
19.2.20, BL-015. **Fast track existed nowhere in the package** — not an enum value, not a description, not a screen.
**An attribute of the entitlement rather than a queue class or a product kind**, because the same ride serves standby and fast-track guests from one capacity: `queue` already has `isFastPass` on an entry and needed something to read it from.

entriesAllowed.description: Null means unlimited. The Fast Pass consumption counter lives here.

transportRestriction.description: **The journey a transport pass is good for** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-21). Set on the template `transport.createTransportPassType` creates, from the station pair the guest bought the pass for, and copied to the entitlement. `access` refuses a boarding scan whose departure does not serve both stations in a direction the restriction allows, and consumes one of `entriesAllowed` per boarding. Null on every other template.

bothDirections.description: Valid from either station to the other, as the prototype sells it.

routeIds.description: The routes it may be used on. Empty means any active route serving both stations.

purchaseEligibility.description:
1.1.38, 1.1.121, 1.1.125, 1.1.126. **`admissionRulesId` governs where an entitlement admits, not who may buy it**, and `promotions.evaluatePromotions` gates a discount rather than a sale. Neither refuses a purchase.
**Evaluated at add-to-cart, not at checkout.** A guest told at payment that they cannot buy a resident rate has already entered a card.

minHeightCm.description: **Height gates a ride and can gate a sale.** A ticket sold to somebody who cannot ride it is a refund at the gate.

requiresVerification.description: **Whether the claim is checked or taken on trust.** A resident rate sold unverified and refused at the gate is worse than one that could not be bought.

personType.description:
2.11.7. **Adult, child and senior existed only as `ProductVariant.axisValues` — a variant axis rather than an attribute of the holder.** So changing a child ticket to an adult one was an exchange to a different product, and an upgrade that should be a price difference became a cancel-and-rebuy.
Recorded here as well as on the variant, because **the guest ages and the product does not.**

canShareMedia.description: Whether this entitlement may be appended to media a guest already holds (CF-58). False for anything surrendered at use — a single-entry ticket taken at the gate is not a claim token for a locker bought afterwards.

canClaimShopAndDrop.description: Whether this entitlement may be scanned to claim goods left under 4.4.7. False for a single-entry ticket that is surrendered at the gate — a claim token the guest no longer holds is not a claim token.

isNameBound.description: True requires a holder name at sale. Most entitlements carry none — identity and entitlement are separate concerns.

autoRenewDefault.description: **Taken from their `membership_plan`, 20 September — the "take those" half of the TAKE BODY verdict.** `identity.customer_membership.auto_renew` carries the flag per holder and nothing said what it should start as.

renewalTermDays.description: What a renewal extends the membership by. `orders.membership_renewal` records `previousExpiryAt` and `newExpiryAt` and **the number between them lived nowhere**.

renewalGraceDays.description: How long after expiry a membership can still be renewed rather than rejoined. `membership_renewal.failureReason` implies a window and there was none, so a failed card on the expiry date had no defined consequence.

renewalVariantId.description: **What a renewal sells, which is usually not what joining sold.** A first-year price and a renewal price are different products, and pointing both at one variant makes a loyalty discount unrepresentable. Null means renewal sells the same thing.

crossesCells.description: True propagates a redemption right to other cells on issue (ADR-0010).

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `venue` scope.** Set by the server, never taken from a body.

GeneratedConfiguration.x-ticvai-persistence: none — a draft, applied through the owning contract; the draft itself is the ai.proposed_action row named by proposedActionId

proposedActionId.description: **The `ai.proposed_action` row this draft was written as**, and the id `decideProposedAction` takes. Without it a reviewer (BO-598) has a draft and no way to approve it.

payload.description: **Open on purpose: its shape is the request body of `targetOperation` in `targetContract`**, validated against that operation before it is returned — this contract does not restate thirty other contracts' request schemas.

assumptions.description: **What it had to guess.** An admin reviewing a draft needs to know which fields came from what they said and which the assistant chose, or they approve a decision they did not make.

clarificationsNeeded.description: What it could not resolve and should ask about.

planId.description: The one-step `ai.action_plan` the draft was written as (AI design 2.3), readable with `getActionPlan`.

GuestListing.description: **How a product appears to a guest** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). `bookable`: listed and searched while it is on sale, and added to the basket. `infoOnly`: listed and searched with its details, photo and `notBookableLabel` whether or not it is on sale, and **never added to a basket** (`addCartLine` refuses it with `409`); the screen opens its details instead. `hidden`: never listed or searched for a guest, and reachable only where a staff channel sells it. Independent of `isSellable`, which says whether a channel may sell it at all.

GuestMerchandiseItem.description: **What a guest caller of `listMerchandise` receives.** The fields a shop screen shows and the ids a guest needs to reserve or buy, and nothing else: no inventory link, no catalogue variant, no stock count, no serial-number flag. `additionalProperties: false` is the guarantee: a staff field added to `MerchandiseItem` does not reach a guest by default.

isAvailable.description: True when the item is active and in stock at its outlet. An item with no `inventoryItemId` never runs out, so it is available while active.

productVariantId.description: The catalogue Product variant the item sells, which `addCartLine` takes as its `variantId` (added 3 October 2026, CHG-R1S-004: the r1 gate found WEB-033 could not add to the cart from the guest projection; qualified from `variantId` by CHG-GTRB-001, since the glossary bans a bare Variant). An id, not the variant record: price and tax still come from the server.

Journey.description:
22.3.1b to 22.3.10b, CF-137. **A journey is a sequence with branches; a `MessageTrigger` is one step of it.** The trigger already handles *"send this when that happens"* — a journey is what you need when the next message depends on what the guest did about the last one.
Five of the ten requirements are named lifecycles — abandoned cart, membership, loyalty, wallet, birthday. **They are not five features.** Each is a journey with a different entry event and a different set of steps, which is why this is one entity and a template library rather than five contracts.
**Consent is checked at every send, not at entry.** A guest who opts out mid-journey stops receiving, and the journey does not need to know — the same rule `MessageTrigger` follows and the one PDPL Article 17(1) makes unconditional.

templateKind.description: Which named lifecycle this implements. **Set for reporting and for the library**, not for behaviour — the steps decide what happens.

entryEvent.description: 22.3.2b. From the event catalogue, so a journey cannot enter on something nothing publishes.

entryConditions.description: Narrows entry — a segment, a tier, a venue. **Evaluated once at entry**, unlike step conditions.

steps.description: 22.3.1b. What the builder produces. **The visual builder is a frontend over this** — the contract holds the graph and the canvas is a rendering of it.

maxDurationDays.description: **A journey with no end is a guest who never leaves it.** After this, entrants exit wherever they are.

reentryPolicy.description: 22.3.6b. **Abandoned cart is the case that needs this.** A guest who abandons three carts in an hour should not get three recovery sequences, and `never` is wrong too — they may genuinely abandon one next month.

scopePath.description:
**The partition key** (ADR-0005). Added 31 August: the operations that write this table declare a scope and the table carried no column for it — **49 tables were in that state**, so a row could be written at venue scope and then read by anything that could reach the table.

**`scope_path` rather than a specific id** because it is prefix-comparable: `uae.dubai` contains `uae.dubai.marina`, and one index answers every level of the walk.

**Operations write it at `venue` scope.**

JourneyStep.description: One node. **A step either sends, waits, or branches** — three kinds rather than a general graph, because a marketing user drawing an arbitrary graph draws a loop.

templateId.description: For `send`. Channel is resolved from the guest's preference at the moment of sending.

sendTimeMode.description: For `send` (29 September, build pass, group G2; 22.3.19). `optimised` delays the send, after the step is reached, to the recipient's suggested hour from `ai.requestSuggestion` (kind `sendTime`) within the next 24 hours and inside `waitUntil`; no suggestion or AI off sends at once, as `fixed`.

channelMode.description: For `send`. `optimised` tries first the consented channel the send-time suggestion names, then `channelPreference` in order (22.9.16).

channelPreference.description: 22.3.3b. Ordered fallback — email, then SMS, then push. **A guest with no email address does not get an email step**, and the step does not fail, it moves down the list.

waitUntil.description: 22.3.5b. **Business hours, time zone and blackout windows** — a wallet low-balance alert at 3am is a complaint, and the venue's quiet hours are venue configuration rather than a property of this step.

condition.description: 22.3.4b. IF/THEN over guest profile, behaviour and prior steps. **The most common condition is whether the previous message worked** — a recovery sequence must stop when the guest buys.

goalEvent.description: For `goal`. **The event that means this journey worked and the guest should leave it** — a purchase for abandoned cart, a renewal for membership. **Reaching a goal exits immediately**, which is what stops a recovered cart from being chased.

MarketingCampaignVariant.description: One content or subject variant of a campaign, for an A/B test (22.1.17; 29 September, build pass, group G2, from group G1's handoff). Written with its campaign by `createCampaign` and `updateCampaign`.

templateId.description: A different template for this variant; null uses the campaign's `content.templateId`.

splitPercent.description: Share of the test group; null splits evenly.

aiDecisionRecordId.description: The decision record of the `ai.proposeMarketingContent` draft it came from, for `aiDraft`.

description.description: What the item is, in the guest's words. Indexed for guest-app search.

variantId.description: The catalogue variant sold. Price and tax come from there.

inventoryItemId.description: The stock item depleted on sale. Null means the item sells but never runs out, which is almost always a configuration error.

isDroppable.description: **Whether the item may be dropped for later collection** (R8 blocker APPROVALS-TENANCY-C34). True unless the venue sets it false for a chilled, fragile or oversized item; `createShopAndDrop` refuses a sale with such a line, 409 `itemNotDroppable`.

outletId.description: The outlet whose price and stock this is: the asking workstation's outlet, or `outletId` for a caller with none (decided 28 September, audit R215).

sku.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (r8 walk of ticket 27820).

siblingOutlets.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (r8 walk of ticket 27820).
siblingOutlets.description: Stock elsewhere in the venue, so a colleague can be sent.

familyKey.description: **The same product at another location** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-18). Optional. A tenant that sells one attraction at several venues gives each venue's product the same key, e.g. `aquarium-entry`; the key names the family across the tenant and each venue has at most one product in it, so a second product at the same venue with the key is refused with `409 duplicate-code`. **What it is for:** when a guest changes location on the booking screen (the 'Booking at' switcher, `BookingFlowConfig.locationSwitcher`), lines whose product shares a `familyKey` with a product at the new venue are carried over to that product, with times and prices refreshed; every other line is cleared. Null means the product belongs to no family and its lines always clear on a switch. Compared case-insensitively, like `code`.

nameLocalised.description: **The product's name in each language the venue sells in** (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011), keyed by ISO 639-1 code, e.g. `{"en": "Aquarium entry", "ar": "دخول الأكواريوم"}`. Every guest surface shows the entry for the guest's language and falls back to `name`, which stays the name staff search and reports print. Null, or a language missing from it, means `name` is shown. At most 200 characters per language, as `name`.

descriptionLocalised.description: The product's description in each language, as `nameLocalised`; falls back to `description` (6 October 2026, CHG-R4-011).

createdByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).
createdByPrincipalId.description: 1.4.18. **The approval gate refuses an approver who is the author, and nothing recorded either.** `SeatBlock`, `DelegatedAccess` and `ManualDiscountRequest` all carry this and the product passing through approval did not.

approvedByPrincipalId.x-ticvai-staff-only: Omitted from the response when the caller is a guest or a visitor (R164).

responsibleDepartmentId.description: Who owns this product commercially. A scope node at `department` level.

onSaleFrom.description: 1.4.8. **A seasonal product should not need somebody awake at midnight.** Archiving already runs on a timer in this contract, so the machinery exists; `effectiveFrom` appears on tax codes, FX rates and white-label policies and not here.

onSaleTo.description: Retires the product automatically. **Retirement is not deletion** — the product stops selling and every order that referenced it still resolves.

categoryId.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product` and `retail.product`, 20 September.** `catalogue.product_category` has existed since 20 August with two operations and nothing could be filed under it — a merchandise hierarchy with a tree and no leaves. Their per-domain product tables both carried this column and ours did not.

isSellable.description:
True only when live **and** carried by a published bundle. Approval and publication are different acts.
**Derived, never set.** It changes when `transitionProductLifecycle` moves the product and when `publishBundle` carries it, so `updateProduct` does not take it — `withdraw` is how a product stops selling.

isStockTracked.description: **Taken from their `fnb.product`, 20 September.** Whether a sale decrements stock, which is not what `isSellable` asks. A ticket is sellable and tracks no stock; a bottle of water is both. Without it, an F&B sale cannot tell inventory whether to move.

segmentTags.description:
7.3.5. **A channel and a segment tag are mandatory and nothing required either.** A catalogue that cannot be filtered by segment is a catalogue nobody can report on.
**Hierarchical, not flat** — `family/with-toddlers` narrows `family` without duplicating it, which is how the promotions engine already treats scope.
**A level is a tag under `level/`** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-19): `level/beginner`, `level/intermediate`, `level/advanced`, `level/expert` (proposed codes, client to correct). A guest screen filters on it with `listProducts` `segmentTag`, and the words a guest reads beside each option come from `ProductCategory.description`, not from the tag.

codeSchema.description:
7.3.4 specifies `[ParkCode]-[ProductType]-[Variant]`. **`Product.code` existed and nothing required a format**, so a venue with three thousand products had three thousand conventions.
The tenant sets the pattern and the platform generates against it. **Validation is the point, not the string** — a code typed by hand is a code that will not sort.

entitlementTemplateId.description: What the buyer receives. Null for products that grant nothing — F&B and retail. Identity and entitlement are separate concerns.

blockedOffline.description: True for seated and retail. Seated because a seat map is not a count; retail because stock depletes in real time.

dataMaskValues.description: Custom fields. JSONB-backed, defined by the venue's data mask.

notBookableLabel.description: The label a guest reads on an `infoOnly` product, e.g. *Info only* or *Not bookable online; ask at the desk* (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-14). Each value at most 60 characters. Null means the guest screen shows its default wording. Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

salesContact.description: **Who a guest contacts to book a view-only product** (decided 29 September, W3), e.g. a training course listed with full details and no Book button. Shown as *Call sales* and *Email sales* on an `infoOnly` product. Null means the venue's own contact (white-label `getTenantAppStatus.contact`). Ignored unless `guestListing` is `infoOnly`.

bookingFlowId.description: **The booking flow this product is sold through** (decided 29 September, W8 and W12): a white-label `BookingFlow` of the venue, which orders the guest's steps (for a workshop, the product first and then the date and time). Null means the category's flow (`ProductCategory.bookingFlowId`), and failing that the venue's flow for the product's `kind`. Written by `createProduct` and `updateProduct`, which refuse an id that is not a flow of the venue with `422`.

displayTags.description:
**Short facts a guest reads on the ticket card and under *Read more***: *2 Hours*, *Min 1.10 m*, *Free adult entry*, *Valid 90 days*, *Emirates ID* (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). Not `segmentTags`, which are for reporting and segmentation and which a guest never reads.
**Derived on read when none are set.** When the venue has written no tags, a read returns tags derived from the product's duration (`clock`), entitlement validity (`calendar`) and the eligibility rule's `minHeightCm` (`height`), each marked `derived: true`; they are never stored. Once the venue writes any tag, only what it wrote is returned. Whether the guest screen shows them is `BookingFlowConfig.ticketTags` (white-label).

media.description:
**The product's own photos and video** (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). *Read more* opens on the `isPrimary` item, and a listing shows each product's primary image, so two tickets in one category no longer share the category's picture (`ProductCategory.imageAssetId`).
Every `assetId` names an asset of the asset library (`assets.yaml` `MediaAsset`) in status `ready` whose kind matches `kind`; anything else is a `422`. **Exactly one item is `isPrimary`** when the list is not empty, and an `assetId` appears once; otherwise `400`. Setting the list records each reference as asset usage (`MediaUsage` with `surface: product`, `referenceId` the product id, `isLive` true while the product is listed to guests), which is what stops a used asset being archived from under the product.

consentQuestionIds.description: **The consent questions a guest answers when booking this product**, in the order they are asked (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-26): *Are you able to swim?*, *Do you hold a scuba certification?*, *I accept the risk*. Each id names a consent question defined in marketing-crm (`ConsentQuestion`), which owns the text, its version and whether it is asked per person or once per booking; the answer is stored there as a consent record (question version, answer, who answered, when). **One question or several, as the venue chooses.** A flow can carry its own list too (`white-label.BookingFlow.settings.consentQuestionIds`, on the product's published booking flow as `getPublishedBookingFlow` resolves it: product, then category, then the venue's flow for the kind; moved from `BookingFlowConfig` 29 September, W12); a booking asks the union of the flow's questions and those of every product in the cart, each question once (`orders.Cart.consentQuestions`). An id that names no active consent question of the tenant is a `422`.

requiresTimeWindow.description: **True for a space sold by the hour**, e.g. a meeting room type (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-13). The product is the room type (*focus pod*, *majlis*, *boardroom*, *auditorium*), never a named room; its lengths are a `length` axis (`setProductAttributes`) whose values carry `durationMinutes`, and each length is a variant priced on its own in the price list, so price is the room rate for that length. The cart line carries the booked start and end (orders), the end being the start plus the chosen variant's `durationMinutes`; `resources.listProductStartTimes` supplies the start times for a variant and a date and `allocateResources` picks the room from the product's resource requirements (`setExperienceResourceRequirements`) at checkout. True requires every active variant to have a `durationMinutes`; otherwise `422`.

productOwnerPrincipalId.description: The product owner (29 September, data model DM3), set with `setProductContextOwnership`. `responsibleDepartmentId` is the owning department.

operationalContact.description: A principal id or a name, as the context screen takes it.

brandId.description: The brand, as the context screen names it (a catalogue brand category).

eventId.description: **The event this product sells admission to** (4 October 2026, CHG-FXC-011; WEB-002, WEB-004): a product page finds its event and the event's performances (`Performance.eventId`) give it dates. Null for a product not tied to an event (merchandise, a pass, a membership).

ProductCategory.description:
Retail Board 2 of the client's design set, 20 August. **`listSeatCategories` existed and a product category did not** — a seat category prices a seat, and a merchandise hierarchy groups a catalogue.
**Brand sits here rather than as its own entity.** A venue with four brands and a hierarchy five levels deep can express that with a parent; a venue with one brand should not have to maintain a table containing one row.
**`displayOrder` is not alphabetical and that is the point.** A retail category list runs in the order the merchandiser wants a guest to see it, and sorting by name puts *Accessories* above *Apparel* forever.

code.description:
**Taken from their category tables, 20 September.** Ours had a uuid and a localised name, so an importer matching *Beverages* had to match on a display string that a venue is free to translate.
**Unique per tenant where set** (decided 28 September, audit R108): two categories in one tenant never share a code, and `setProductCategories` refuses a body that would, with `409 duplicate-code`.

parentId.description: **One tree, not four.** A brand under a department under a category is how a real merchandise hierarchy runs, and separate tables for each level cannot express a venue that nests them differently.

scopePath.description: Set by the server from the venue the caller acts at; not sent.

description.description: The short line a guest reads under a category option, e.g. *Surf lessons: learn on the beginner wave with a coach* (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-19). Each language value at most 200 characters.

bookingFlowId.description: **The booking flow for every product filed here** that names none of its own (decided 29 September, W12, BO-115). Null means the venue's flow for each product's `kind`. A white-label `BookingFlow` of the venue; `setProductCategories` refuses any other id with `422`.

isActive.description: **Deactivated rather than deleted.** A category with a season behind it still names the products sold under it, and removing it rewrites last year's report.

ProductCategoryNode.description: **One node of the tree `listProductCategories` returns.** A `ProductCategory` with its children nested under it, in `displayOrder`, so no caller reassembles the hierarchy from `parentId`. `setProductCategories` still takes the flat list, because a write names each parent by id.

ProductDisplayTag.description: One short fact on a ticket card (decided 29 September, 23SEP-3). `kind` picks the icon.

kind.description: `clock` a duration, `height` a height rule, `free` something included free, `calendar` a validity, `id` a document the guest must bring.

label.description: What the guest reads, e.g. *2 Hours*. Each language value at most 40 characters.

derived.description: True on a tag the server derived on read because the venue set none. Never sent.

ProductKind.description:
**`openDated` added 24 August** from the client's *Create Ticket Flow* board, which names six main ticket types and this was the one with no kind: **valid on any date within an eligible range, rather than for a named performance or a fixed date.**
The mechanism already existed — `access.entitlement` carries `valid_from`, `valid_to`, `entries_allowed` and `frozen_days`, which is exactly an open-dated pass. **What was missing was the product saying it is one**, so a catalogue could not offer it and a report could not count it.
**`datedAdmission` is a different thing and the two were being conflated**: dated is *this Tuesday*, open-dated is *any Tuesday between March and June*. A guest buying the second and being sold the first has bought the wrong ticket.
**Transport uses two existing kinds, not a new one** (decided 29 September, rev 3 REV3-21). A one-way trip is `timedAdmission`: `transport.createTransportRoute` creates the route's product with one variant per passenger type, and each departure is a performance. A multi-trip or unlimited pass is `openDated`: `transport.createTransportPassType` creates it, with `EntitlementTemplate.entriesAllowed` = the pass's trips (null for unlimited), the validity = `validityDays`, and `EntitlementTemplate.transportRestriction` naming the station pair the pass was bought for, so `access` refuses it on another journey. The sale path is unchanged: both are cart lines, priced by `transport.quoteTransportFare` (orders `TransportLineAttributes`).

**`walletTopUp` added 20 October 2026** (r8 re-walk, CHG-R8RW-001): the product a wallet top-up is sold as, so the money for a top-up is taken on an order like any other sale and `createPayment` has its `orderId`. A venue has one, with one variant. Orders prices its line at the line's `quotedUnitPrice` (the amount being loaded; no tax, since stored value is a liability and not a supply), and the line may share a sale with anything else (the client-approved till's "Add top-up to sale", CHG-R8RW-009); once the order is paid, wallet `topUpWallet` credits that line's amount, once per line. A value added to a response enum, so a breaking change under ADR-0026, approved as BC-460 to BC-462; a client that does not know it shows the product as a plain product.

ProductMedia.description: One photo or video of a product, referencing the asset library (decided 29 September, 23SEP-4). One row per product and asset, so the asset library can answer which products use an asset.

isPrimary.description: The item *Read more* opens on and a listing shows. Exactly one per product.

ProductSalesContact.description: Who to contact to book a view-only product (decided 29 September, W3). At least one of `phone` or `email`.

note.description: A line shown under the contact, e.g. *Group courses are booked by phone*. At most 200 characters per language.

definitionVersion.description: The version this ran against. With the parameters and scope below, it is everything needed to reproduce the result.

parameters.description: The parameters it ran with, keyed by `ReportParameter.key` of `definitionVersion` — defaults filled in, so the record is complete.

scopeApplied.description: Scope paths the caller held. What constrained the result.

expiresAt.description: Results are retained for a limited period, then discarded.

ReportResult.x-ticvai-persistence: none — result set, cached in object storage

rows.description: **Open on purpose; the shape is `columns`.** Each row is keyed by `columns[].key`, and each value is of that column's `type` — money as a `Money`, dates, date-times and uuids as strings. A report's columns are chosen at run time, so no fixed schema can name them.

totals.description: Aggregated columns only, keyed and typed as a row is.

dataAsOf.description: Replica position the result was read at. Reporting reads a lag-tolerant replica, so this may trail the primary by seconds — stating it prevents an argument about a figure that moved.

parameters.description: **Open on purpose; its shape is the report's.** Keyed by `ReportParameter.key` of the definition being run, each value of that parameter's `type`. An `isRequired` parameter with no value here and no `defaultValue` is the `400` `runReport` lists.

venueId.description: Narrows to one venue. Omitting it returns everything the caller's scope permits — it cannot be used to reach beyond that.

dateFrom.description: Defaults to today in the venue's time zone when not sent (decided 28 September, audit R158). A business date, closing at the venue's `businessDayCutoff` (tenancy `VenueSettings`, default 00:00; CHG-R6-032).

dateTo.description: Defaults to today in the venue's time zone when not sent (audit R158).

forceAsync.description: Queue regardless of size, for a result to be collected later.

SaleBoard.description: **A board is stored as three tables** (decided 14 October 2026, Chinmay, ADAM CR-080; CHG-TEN-001): the board (`platform.sale_board`), one row per page (`pages[]`, `platform.sale_board_page`, keyed to the board) and one row per tile (`pages[].tiles[]`, `platform.sale_board_tile`, keyed to its page by a NOT NULL `sale_board_page_id`, so a tile follows its page's row-level security). Until then the persistence named the board alone, and the tile table held an id and a nullable page key and nothing a till could draw.

code.description: Unique within the venue (as the hand-written r0 table had it). A second board with the same code is `409 duplicate-code` (audit R108; ADAM CR-080; CHG-TEN-001).

SaleBoardTile.description:
**One button on one page of a till board** (ADAM CR-080, 14 October 2026; CHG-TEN-001): the rows of `SaleBoard.pages[].tiles[]`, each keyed to its page. A position holds one tile on a page (`x-ticvai-unique-together`).
**A tile that acts names what it acts on** (`x-ticvai-required-when`, carried as a CHECK): a `product` tile names its variant, a `category` tile the catalogue category it opens, an `action` tile the till action it runs (`actionCode`); a `spacer` names nothing. The hand-written r0 table had the product rule as `sale_board_tile_product` ("a product tile with no variant is a button that does nothing", handoff/storage-design.md).
**A tile's variant is checked when the board is saved and again when it is published.** `createSaleBoard` and `updateSaleBoard` ask Catalogue whether every product tile's variant is sellable at the board's venue (`catalogue#variantsSellableAt`, ADAM CR-081); `publishBundle` leaves out a tile whose product is not `isSellable` when the bundle is cut, and the till never draws it.

variantId.description: The catalogue variant a `product` tile sells (`catalogue.variant`). Required when `kind` is `product`.

categoryId.description: **The catalogue category a `category` tile opens** (`catalogue.product_category`; ADAM CR-080, CHG-TEN-001). Required when `kind` is `category`; until 14 October a category tile referenced nothing.

actionCode.description: **The till action an `action` tile runs** (ADAM CR-080, CHG-TEN-001). Required when `kind` is `action`. The values are the sell screen's own actions (POS-002 hold and recall, discount, guest lookup, media scan, receipt reprint); proposed, client to correct. Until 14 October an action tile referenced nothing.

colour.description: `#rrggbb`, as the hand-written r0 table held it (`char(7)`; audit R246; CHG-TEN-001).

SerialisedItem.description:
Retail Board 4 of the client's design set, 20 August. **`StockBatch` was added on 18 August with a lot number, and serialisation to the individual item is a step beyond it.**
A lot answers *which delivery did this come from*. A serial answers *where is this exact one* — which is what a jewellery counter, a phone, a ticketed collectible or anything with a warranty needs.
**Most stock is not serialised and should not be.** Turning it on for a 2 AED keyring creates a row per keyring, so it is a per-item decision rather than a policy.

batchId.description: The batch it arrived in, where the item is both lotted and serialised.

serial.description: **Unique within the item, not globally.** Two manufacturers reuse serial numbers and a global constraint would refuse the second one.

soldOnOrderLineId.description: **The link that makes serialisation worth having.** A warranty claim, a recall and a proof of purchase all start with *which sale was this exact item*.

UpdateDonationCampaignRequest.x-ticvai-persistence: none — request only; a partial update of catalogue.donation_campaign
UpdateDonationCampaignRequest.description: **A partial update of DonationCampaign** (the CR-089 pattern; CHG-SHP-008): `updateDonationCampaign` sends only what changes, and a field left out keeps its stored value. Nothing is required and nothing has a default, so a generated client never resends a value it did not mean to change. The server's own fields (id, raisedTotal) are not sendable.

beneficiary.description: Who the money is for. Shown to the guest, and it is the reason they give.

liabilityAccountId.description: **Donations post here, not to revenue** (1.1.132). Money collected for a charity is not the venue's to recognise, and treating it as revenue is a restatement waiting to happen.

channels.description: 1.1.133. Where it may be solicited — POS, kiosk, web, app.

UpdateEntitlementTemplateRequest.description: **What `updateEntitlementTemplate` may change** (CHG-R6-040). Each field means what it means on `EntitlementTemplate`; only the fields sent change. `code` is not here: it is fixed once created. Blackout dates are set with `setEntitlementTemplateBlackoutDates`, and archiving with `archiveEntitlementTemplate`.

regionId.description: The region that owns the rule. Upsell rules are owned at region and read at venue (decided 28 September, audit R183); set from the caller's region scope on create.

scopePath.description: **The partition key** (ADR-0005): the owning region's path, set with `regionId` on create. Row-level security reads the rule at and beneath it (`x-ticvai-rls: read-beneath`, CHG-GEN-005), so a venue reads its region's rules, and only the region or above writes them. **Always present, never null** (CHG-R6G-002): the column is NOT NULL once the rules that predate it are backfilled from `region_id` through `platform.scope.path` (handoff/migration-review.md).

channels.description: Empty applies to every channel. Restriction is opt-in — a rule that fires on the website but not at a counter is a guest experience inconsistency.

outletId.description: **The outlet this till stands in** (CHG-CSP-006). Its board is the till's board unless the till overrides it. Null on a workstation that belongs to no outlet (a ticket office counter set up before outlets), which must then carry its own board.

saleBoard.description:
Determines which front end loads. Bound to the workstation, not the role — the F&B terminal opens the F&B board. What the operator may then DO within it is governed by their permissions.
**The effective board** since 2 October 2026 (DEC-183; CHG-CSP-006): the till's own when it overrides the outlet, otherwise the outlet's (`saleBoardSource`).
**Resolved on read, never copied** (decided 20 October 2026, Chinmay, R8 blocker cause APPROVALS-TENANCY-C39, option A; CHG-R8SPN-013). `platform.workstation.sale_board` holds only this till's own override and is null when `saleBoardSource` is `outlet`. `getWorkstation`, `listWorkstations` and `configureWorkstation`'s answer build `saleBoard` from the override when there is one, otherwise from the outlet's `platform.outlet.sale_board_id` and that `platform.sale_board` row (its id, kind and name). So `updateOutlet` and `updateSaleBoard` change what every inheriting till shows with no write to `platform.workstation`, and no stored copy can go stale.

saleBoardSource.description: **Where `saleBoard` came from** (decided 2 October 2026, Chinmay, BO-109: "Per outlet, with a till override"; DEC-183; CHG-CSP-006): `outlet` when the till uses its outlet's layout, `workstation` when this till overrides it. BO-109 shows which tills differ from their outlet.

cashDrawerLimit.description: **This till's drawer limit, overriding the venue's** (`VenueSettings.cashDrawerLimit`; DEC-179; CHG-CSP-016). Null inherits the venue's. Above it the till warns and offers a cash lift.

cashierInputMode.description: BL-061. **How the cashier at this till enters a sale**, as `configureWorkstation` set it. Stored on the workstation and returned here since 14 October 2026 (ADAM CR-082; CHG-TEN-003): until then the request took it and nothing kept it.

guestDisplayContent.description: BL-061. **What the guest-facing screen shows while a sale is in progress**, as `configureWorkstation` set it. Stored on the workstation and returned here since 14 October 2026 (ADAM CR-082; CHG-TEN-003).

accessPointId.description: Inherited from the workstation, never selected by the operator. Null where the workstation is not at an access point.

currency.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else. **Kept on the wire , removed from the table** — a client should not walk a hierarchy to read a figure, and the  database should not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their
 region and keep a stored currency: `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, 
`ledger.account`, `control.partner_agreement`.

currencyScale.description:
**Resolved from the region, not stored** (ADR-0018, 24 August). Region-scoped and not overri dable below, so a row in a UAE region is AED and cannot be anything else — storing it per ro w is a copy of a fact that cannot differ. **Kept on the wire, removed from the table**: a cl ient reading a figure should not walk a hierarchy to know what it means, and the database sh ould not hold nine million copies of AED. Four tables genuinely differ from their region and
 keep a stored currency — `orders.payment.tender_currency`, `inventory.supplier`, `ledger.ac
count`, `control.partner_agreement`. **A guest paying USD at an AED venue is a real row; a w orkstation with its own currency is a misconfiguration.**

healthScore.description:
Board 1 of the client's POS set. **A number a manager can sort by** — the package held `lastHeartbeatAt` and a heartbeat timestamp is not a score.
The client's board shows 1,248 workstations at 96% healthy, and **the value of that figure is that it ranks**: a fleet dashboard exists so somebody can open the worst one first.
**Derived from its devices, its heartbeat age, its firmware currency and its error rate.** Read-only, because a workstation that could set its own score would.
**The formula, proposed, client to correct (audit R096 (2)):** score = 40% device online share (the share of its devices reporting online) + 25% heartbeat freshness (100 at one minute old or less, 0 at 15 minutes or more, linear between) + 20% firmware and profile currency (100 on the latest, 50 one version behind, 0 older) + 15% error rate (100 at 0 errors an hour, 0 at 10 or more, linear between), rounded to a whole number. **Below 80 is a warning and below 60 a failure.**

configurationProfileId.description:
Which profile this workstation runs, and at which version. **The client's board shows a fleet split four ways — 72% latest, 18.8% one behind, 6.1% outdated** — and the package had a firmware version field and no profile.
**A profile is what a venue changes; a version is what it deploys.** Conflating them means a venue cannot say *roll the ticketing counters back and leave the kiosks*.

configurationProfileVersion.description: The version of `configurationProfileId` this workstation runs, written when a deployment reaches it; null with no profile (R8 blocker APPROVALS-TENANCY-C08, CHG-R8MIG-019).

offlineCapable.description: Derived from `deploymentProfile`. False only for `thin`. Under local-first, catalogue READS are always local on transactional surfaces; this flag governs whether WRITES can be queued.
